newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish central bank sells crowns for marks.
newsitem.headline: Danish central bank sells crowns for marks.

text.p: Denmark's central bank has been selling Danish crowns at around 3.8090 to the mark in an operation to curb the Danish currency's burgeoning strength, dealers said on Friday.
"The National Bank has bought marks, partly through a broker and partly direct from the banks," a currency dealer told Reuters, adding that such intervention was not unusual.

"The National Bank, in a very professional manner, has from time to time throughout the past year been in the market at the top and bottom, lately mostly at the bottom," he said, referring to the falling mark against the crown.

Over the past two months the crown has firmed by about one percent relative to the mark, fuelled in part by recent purchases by the Norwegian central bank, rising above its EMS central rate of 3.8144 to the mark.
At 1120 GMT it traded in Copenhagen at 3.8100.
The dealer did not believe that the stronger crown would, on its own, lead the central bank to cut the repo rate but said that Denmark would be compelled to follow a German reduction.

"The bank looks more at the effective crown rate, which has in fact fallen over the past couple of days, but if the Bundesbank cuts rates the National Bank will follow," he said. --Per Bech Thomsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
